subject: Service window & latency-floor addendum request — Sapphire Integrations
messages:
From: Alex Ho <alex.ho@sapphire-int.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@sapphire-int.com
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity: service window & latency-floor request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Sapphire Integrations is moving toward a reserved-GPU commitment for inference (we're evaluating a 3-month Dedicated pool). Before we sign, procurement and engineering need an addendum that covers two items:

1) A "service window" carveout: our nightly batch (02:00–05:00 UTC) requires deterministic concurrency and cannot be preempted. Can Redwood provide a hard carveout or a soft-guarantee during that window (we can accept limited burst tokens or credits)?

2) A latency-floor commitment for interactive traffic during business hours (13:00–21:00 UTC): we need an SLO that if 95th percentile tail latency exceeds X ms for more than Y minutes we get an automatic fallback to a pinned model variant and a credit mechanism.

Attached is a short PDF with usage patterns and required thresholds.

Can you propose language we can include in the order form or addendum? Also looping in procurement (procurement@sapphire-int.com).

Thanks,
Alex Ho
Head of Platform Engineering
Sapphire Integrations

Attachment: Sapphire_Service_Window_Req.pdf (1 page)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ho <alex.ho@sapphire-int.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 18:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: service window & latency-floor request

Hi Alex — appreciate the clear ask and the usage doc.

High-level proposal we can push now (will follow with a draft addendum):
- Nightly service window (02:00–05:00 UTC): soft carveout with a guaranteed minimum of N reserved slots for your pool (configurable), plus burst tokens for X minutes/day. If preemption occurs beyond agreed thresholds, credits apply.
- Interactive latency floor: 95th percentile tail SLO with automatic routing to pinned model variant if breached for >10 minutes; credit ladder tied to minutes over threshold.

I'm looping in our pricing and product leads to align on the credit ladder and exact wording. Expect a draft addendum and queueing-runbook within 24 hours.

Next steps:
- Confirm the exact 95th percentile threshold (you suggested 450ms in the doc — is that still accurate?)
- Are you OK with a soft carveout (reserved slots + burst token model) or do you require an absolute hard isolation?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_dedicated_addendum_v1.pdf (placeholder)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: service window & latency-floor request

Jordan — quick internal notes before we send the draft to Sapphire: 

- Hard carveout is operationally risky; recommend proposing soft carveout: reserve 6 slots for 02:00–05:00 UTC with an additional 15 minutes/day of burst tokens. This aligns with similar deals.
- Latency SLO: clarify they asked for 95th percentile tail — implement as P95 (P99 would be too strict operationally). Propose threshold 450ms P95 for interactive model (per their doc). Credits: 5% invoice credit for each contiguous 10-minute window breach up to 30%/month cap.
- Need ops-runbook attachment (queueing_runbook_draft.md) and clear escalation path — include on-call rotation and contact points (CS + Infra).

Ben — from a commercial standpoint, we can accept credits but require minimum committed spend of $120k/mo and 90-day term. Thoughts?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: queueing_runbook_draft.md

---

Ben Carter (inline reply): SGTM on the commercial floor; confirm you want me on the signature loop.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ho <alex.ho@sapphire-int.com>
Cc: procurement@sapphire-int.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: service window & latency-floor request

Hi Alex — attaching the draft addendum and runbook per our internal alignment. Summary of what's in the doc: 

- Nightly service window (02:00–05:00 UTC): soft carveout — 6 reserved slots + 15-minute burst token per day. Preemption beyond agreed thresholds triggers invoice credits (see section 3).
- Interactive latency floor: P95 ≤ 450ms; automatic fallback to pinned variant after 10 continuous minutes over threshold. Credit ladder: 5% per 10-minute breach, capped at 30%/month.
- Commercial: 90-day committed term, $120k/mo minimum. DocuSign link below for addendum and order form.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/signer/SAPPH-2025-09
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Please review and let us know any redlines. If you approve, we'll route for signature and provision the reserved slots in 3 business days post-signature.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_addendum_v1.pdf
